confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors rest on five searches (summaries, not full page reads). Numbeo-based figures were about $20 for an inexpensive meal and $80-$90 for a mid-range three-course meal for two. Numbeo had a $7.00 draft pint, and the Toast Denver median was $7.02 (Mar 2026). Cappuccino was $5.66-$6.09 on Numbeo, against mostly $3.75-$5.50 on undated independent cafe menus. The cocktail uses Expatistan's roughly $16 downtown-club estimate (which the site calls a guess) and a roughly 2x-beer relationship. Wine by the glass had no Denver average, so it is set at roughly 1.65x beer and loosely cross-checked against scattered $9-$10 happy-hour glasses, which makes it the weakest drink anchor. Accommodation is a holistic July high-season estimate from general knowledge. No accommodation searches were run and no live listings were inspected. Denver has few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain. FX is the RBA USD-per-AUD rate dated 18 Nov 2026, as reported in RBA page content returned by search.
comparable_city_reasoning: Denver-specific sources were used for food and drink, with no substitute city. Accommodation is a holistic estimate by analogy with other mid-to-upper-priced US western metros (e.g., Portland, Austin, Salt Lake City), treating July as summer high season.
